questions.question: 1. Diseases such as cancers, osteoarthritis, muscular dystrophy and multiple sclerosis are all example of:
questions.answer_guide: These are non-infectious diseases caused by gradual deterioration of body tissues – degenerative diseases.

questions.question: 2. Site of infection/attack of Hepatitis B is
questions.answer_guide: Hepatitis B virus attacks the liver.

questions.question: 3. Cholera disease can be treated by taking
questions.answer_guide: Cholera is treated by oral/IV rehydration plus antibiotics such as tetracycline.

questions.question: 4. Factors/Causes of livestock disease such as bone fractures and hemia in scrotum are:
questions.answer_guide: Fractures and hernia result from physical injuries.

questions.question: 5. The methods of livestock handling in which male testicles are made nonfictional is known as:
questions.answer_guide: Making the testes non-functional is castration.

questions.question: 6. The disease that can affect only a particular sex of animal is
questions.answer_guide: Mastitis is inflammation of the udder/mammary gland, so it affects females only.

questions.question: 7. Which class of immurroglobullins does the following diagram show you?

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 220 110" width="100%" style="max-width:220px" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Schematic of an immunoglobulin molecule"><g stroke="#111" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"><path d="M20,22 L95,40 V100" stroke-width="8"/><path d="M38,12 L105,28" stroke-width="5"/><path d="M200,22 L125,40 V100" stroke-width="8"/><path d="M182,12 L115,28" stroke-width="5"/></g></svg>
diagram.caption: Schematic of an immunoglobulin molecule as printed: two heavy chains, each with a light chain alongside, forming a Y-shaped antibody.

questions.answer_guide: The diagram shows a single Y-shaped (monomer) antibody with two heavy and two light chains – the typical IgG shape.

questions.question: 8. Immunity developed by vaccination is an example of
questions.answer_guide: A vaccine makes the body produce its own antibodies – artificial active immunity.

questions.question: 9. Which of the following is a disaccharide?
questions.answer_guide: Sucrose (glucose + fructose) is a disaccharide; the others are polysaccharides.

questions.question: 10. Which of the following bases is NOT found in RNA?
questions.answer_guide: RNA contains uracil instead of thymine.

questions.question: 11. Change of a chromosomal structure that occurs when the genes appear more than once on the same chromosome is known as
questions.answer_guide: Repetition of a chromosome segment is duplication.

questions.question: 12. Which of the following cell organelles are responsible for muscle contraction?
questions.answer_guide: Muscle contraction is produced by the sliding of actin and myosin filaments.

questions.question: 13. Taking in a whole food material and breaking inside the body is known as
questions.answer_guide: Ingesting whole food and digesting it internally is holozoic nutrition.

questions.question: 14. The other name(s) for Krebs cycle is/are
questions.answer_guide: The Krebs cycle is also called the citric acid cycle and the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle.

questions.question: 15. Which of the correct sequence of parts the human alimentary canal?
options: a. Mouth → Stomach → Small intestine → Esophagus
b. Mouth → Esophagus → Stomach → Small intestine
c. Mouth → Small Intestine → Esophagus → Stomach
d. Mouth → Small intestine → Stomach → Esophagus
questions.answer_guide: Mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine.

questions.question: 16. People of blood group “O” are:
questions.answer_guide: Group O red cells have no A or B antigens, so O people are universal donors.

questions.question: 17. Which of the following bones is part of appendicular skeleton?
questions.answer_guide: The humerus is a limb bone (appendicular); the others are axial.

questions.question: 18. Oxygenated blood leaving the ventricle is carried by
questions.answer_guide: The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle.

questions.question: 19. The outermost layer that is made of white tough protective fibers around the eyes and forms the cornea at the front is called:
questions.answer_guide: The sclera is the tough white outer coat, continuous with the cornea at the front.

questions.question:
1.
  a. Define a Pathogen. (2marks)
  b. Differentiate between air-born disease and contagious borne diseases. (2marks)
  c. Explain the symptoms amoebic diseases. (2marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. A pathogen is a disease-causing organism (micro-organism) such as a virus, bacterium, protozoan or fungus.
b. Air-borne diseases spread through the air in droplets released by coughing or sneezing (e.g. TB, influenza); contagious diseases spread by direct physical contact with an infected person or their belongings (e.g. ringworm, scabies).
c. Amoebic dysentery (amoebiasis): diarrhoea with blood and mucus, abdominal pain/cramps, fever, dehydration, loss of weight and fatigue.

questions.question:
2. The following table represents infectious diseases. Complete the blank spaces (6marks)

   | Disease  | Causual agent (pathogen) | Mode of transmission           |
   | A ...... | Virus                    | Through in haling infected air |
   | B Malaria| Protozoan (Plasmodium)   | ..........                     |
   | C Syphilis| ..........              | Through sexual intercourse     |
questions.answer_guide:
A – Influenza (common cold/flu) [also accept measles or COVID-19]
B – Through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito
C – Bacterium (Treponema pallidum)

questions.question:
3.
  A) Mention any two general signs and symptoms of parasite infestation. (2marks)
     a. ........
     b. ........
  B) Give two examples of Ectoparasites (2marks)
     a. ........
     b. ........
  C) State two methods of controlling roundworms (2marks)
     a. ........
     b. ........
questions.answer_guide:
A) Any two: loss of weight/poor growth; anaemia; itching and skin irritation; diarrhoea or abdominal pain; loss of appetite; general weakness.
B) Any two: ticks, lice, fleas, mites (mange), tsetse flies.
C) Any two: deworming with anthelmintic drugs; washing hands before eating and after using the toilet; proper disposal of faeces/using latrines; washing fruits and vegetables and cooking food properly; drinking clean, boiled water.

questions.question:
4.
  a. Classify the living organism which cause livestock disease into two groups by filling the empty boxes. (2marks)
  b. Enlist any two general signs of illness in livestock. (2marks)
  c. Mention any two conditions that pre-dispose livestock animals to disease, or make the animal prone to contact disease. (2marks)

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 520 170" width="100%" style="max-width:520px" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Blank classification chart for living organisms that cause livestock diseases"><rect x="20" y="10" width="480" height="40" fill="#fff" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/><text x="260" y="36" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="normal">Living organisms that cause livestock diseases</text><path d="M260,50 V75 M130,75 H390 M130,75 V100 M390,75 V100" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><rect x="30" y="100" width="200" height="50" fill="#fff" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/><text x="130" y="131" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="normal">........................</text><rect x="290" y="100" width="200" height="50" fill="#fff" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/><text x="390" y="131" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="normal">........................</text></svg>
diagram.caption: Classification chart: 'Living organisms that cause livestock diseases' branching into two empty boxes to be filled in.

questions.answer_guide:
a. Box 1: Micro-organisms / pathogens (viruses, bacteria, protozoa, fungi)
   Box 2: Parasites (endoparasites and ectoparasites)
b. Any two: loss of appetite; dullness and isolation from the herd; rough/dull coat; high temperature (fever); drop in milk production; diarrhoea; abnormal discharges; loss of weight.
c. Any two: poor nutrition/malnutrition; poor housing and hygiene; overcrowding; stress (long transport, extreme weather); age (very young or old); lack of vaccination; mixing with sick animals.

a. A: Plasma cells (secreting antibodies); B: Memory B cells
b. Memory B cells remember the specific antigen and, on re-infection, rapidly divide to produce many plasma cells and antibodies, giving a fast and strong (secondary) response – long-term immunity.
c. The secondary response is faster (and stronger and longer-lasting), because memory cells are already present.

questions.question:
6.
  a) Classify the following defense mechanisms into first, second & third lines of defense interferons, mucus membranes and lymphocytes. (3marks)

     | First line defense | Second line defense | Third line defense |
     |                    |                     |                    |

  b) Explain two ways in which innate immunity and acquired immunity differ? (2marks)
  c) What is chemotaxis? (1mark)
questions.answer_guide:
a) First line: mucus membranes; Second line: interferons; Third line: lymphocytes
b) Any two: innate immunity is present from birth, whereas acquired immunity develops after exposure to antigens or vaccination; innate immunity is non-specific, whereas acquired immunity is specific to a particular antigen; innate immunity has no memory, whereas acquired immunity has memory cells (a faster response on re-infection).
c) Chemotaxis is the movement of cells (e.g. phagocytes/white blood cells) towards or away from a chemical stimulus, such as chemicals released at a site of infection.

questions.question:
7.
  a) Compare between plant cell wall & cell membrane by completing the following table. (2marks)

     | Point of comparison  | Cell wall       | Cell membrane                                   |
     | Existence            | i) ........     | Found in both plant & animal cell               |
     | Chemical composition | ii) ........    | Protein molecules embedded in phospholipid bilayer |
     | Permeability         | Fully permeable | iii) ........                                   |

  b) There are two major types of cells based on the presence of nucleus mention Them. (2marks)
  c) Identify the function of ribosomes (2marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) i) Found only in plant cells (and fungi/bacteria) – not in animal cells
   ii) Cellulose
   iii) Partially (selectively/semi-) permeable
b) Prokaryotic cells (no true nucleus, e.g. bacteria) and eukaryotic cells (with a true nucleus, e.g. plant and animal cells).
c) Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis.

questions.question:
8.
  a) Put the following events of embryonic developing their correct order/sequence starting from the first to last stage: (2marks)
     Implantation, fertilization, birth
  b) Describe the main difference between identical twins and fraternal twins (2marks)
  c) State any two secondary sexual characteristics in girls. (2marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) Fertilization → Implantation → Birth
b) Identical twins develop from one fertilised egg (zygote) that splits into two, so they are genetically identical and the same sex; fraternal twins develop from two different eggs fertilised by two different sperms, so they are genetically different and may be of different sexes.
c) Any two: development of breasts; widening of hips; growth of pubic and underarm hair; start of menstruation; deposition of fat under the skin.

questions.question:
9.
  a) What is the transpiration in plants? (1mark)
  b) List two benefits of transpiration for plants. (2marks)
     I. ........
     II. ........
  c) State the three necessary materials for seed generation (3marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through the stomata of the leaves.
b) Any two: cools the plant; helps pull water and dissolved minerals up from the roots (transpiration pull); keeps cells turgid; distributes mineral salts.
c) (read as seed germination) Water (moisture), oxygen (air) and a suitable (warm) temperature.

questions.question:
10.
  a) Define coordination in living things. (2marks)
  b) Name the two systems that are responsible for body coordination. (2marks)
  c) Explain the difference between community and ecosystem. (2marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) Coordination is the way the different parts of an organism work together in harmony, detecting stimuli and producing suitable responses.
b) The nervous system and the endocrine (hormonal) system.
c) A community is all the populations of different organisms (living things only) living together in one area; an ecosystem is the community together with its non-living (physical) environment, interacting as one unit.
